submitter: bugs_open/410 lane — ROUND 1. bugs_open/410 is a PATTERN file (three seams, three lanes, one week, all failing toward the quiet default, all reporting complete). This submission implements its candidate 3 (make the silent skips countable) for instance 3 only, plus the door-closing ratchet for that class. Candidate 1 (unknown-reason refusal) and candidate 2 (vocabulary/reader parity, bugs_open/404's candidate 0, owned by the 384 lane) are deliberately NOT in scope and are named as such below. The two lanes whose work touches the same file were consulted before any edit: news_editorial handed over the function ('GO FIRST, THE FUNCTION IS YOURS') and bugs_open/399 confirmed no overlapping check. The code is implemented and tested at the time of submission, per this estate's rule that code is not held for a verdict on a shared HEAD; it will carry Council-Submitted until a verdict lands.
rationale:
bugs_open/410 instance 3: loadStoredSections' rows.Scan error branch is Warn-and-continue, so a scan failure returns fewer sections — or none — with NO error. Because save_page_sections then replaces the page's rows WHOLESALE (`DELETE FROM page_components WHERE page_id = $1`, save_page_sections_action.go:898, verified first-hand), a section missing from that slice is not merely unrendered: it is DELETED. The page ships with a hole, under a fresh deploy stamp, with the work item reported complete. Not blank, not erroring, not obviously stale — REBUILT. That asymmetry is why this reader is strict where scanBlogArticles is graded: a listing that loses one post degrades a nav surface; this loses the page.

THIS IS NOT HYPOTHETICAL. Commit bd811fa93 added two columns to that SELECT and SEVEN tests went red, every one reporting a variant of 'expected exactly one section, got 0' and NOT ONE saying 'scan mismatch'. A correct change to a genuine query presented as an empty page rather than an error. Worse, and this is the decisive detail (supplied and verified by the news_editorial lane, who own those tests): those seven assert section COUNT and CONTENT, never rows-in-equals-rows-out, so they would have PASSED on a column change that was wrong in a way that still scanned — and they call mock.ExpectationsWereMet(), so sqlmock's own completeness assertion ran and passed. The query was issued exactly as expected; only the scan silently produced nothing. Even the mocking framework's completeness check cannot see this.

THE FIX IS PROPAGATION OF AN IDIOM THIS PACKAGE ALREADY USES TWICE, BOTH TIMES BECAUSE A REVIEW SEAT REQUIRED IT — not a new mechanism. collectPageSections refuses component grain for a whole page when its canonical reader resolves fewer sections than the metadata held (council round 3ed2b792, bug_historian). scanBlogArticles counts offered against kept across a rows.Scan loop and errors when every offered row failed (council round 170147b4, bug_historian, which REJECTED a first cut that logged-and-skipped unconditionally and documented the exposure in prose without closing it). The loader simply never inherited it.

WHICH COUNT — the intuitive version is the wrong one and the bug file pins it. WRONG: kept vs 'rows in page_components for this page'. That comparison counts tombstones the query deliberately excluded (`build_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'removed'`), so it fires on every page carrying a removed component — a large, healthy population — and a guard that fires constantly on correct input gets loosened within a week. RIGHT: rows the CURSOR YIELDED vs rows KEPT. No second query, so it also cannot race a concurrent writer on a shared tree. In one line: the guard's job is 'did I lose anything the query gave me', not 'does the page have as many components as I expected'.

BLAST RADIUS ON THE FLEET'S BUSIEST PIPELINE — MEASURED AT THE SCAN, AND IT IS ZERO BY SCHEMA RATHER THAN BY LUCK. Every column the loader projects is structurally incapable of failing a scan on today's data: `id uuid NOT NULL`, `position integer NOT NULL`, and every other column either COALESCEd to non-NULL text or scanned into a NULL-safe []byte (content_data, NULL on 54 live rows, scans to nil). Live control [MEASURED 2026-08-26]: `SELECT count(*), count(*) FILTER (WHERE position IS NULL), count(*) FILTER (WHERE content_data IS NULL) FROM page_components WHERE build_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'removed'` returns 2194 | 0 | 54. So the guard CANNOT convert a currently-working rerender into a failing one; it can only speak when the SELECT list and the Scan destinations diverge, which is a code defect introduced by an edit — precisely the edit that turned those seven tests red. This answers the canary/staged-rollout objection directly and better than a canary could: the change is inert on current data BY CONSTRUCTION, not as far as we sampled. Stated limit: this expires the moment the projection or the schema changes; a nullable column added to that SELECT without a COALESCE falsifies it, and the disconfirming query is the one above. The news_editorial lane, whose 035 P1 work adds columns to this SELECT, has been told this is now a constraint on their change and has accepted it.

DELIBERATELY NOT AN ITEM COUNT. An earlier draft leaned on 'page_rerender: 6,428 items, 3 with a reason'. That figure was (a) wrong — site_work_items is a rolling window and across live plus site_work_items_archive it is 203 of 17,285 — and (b) the wrong axis regardless: it counts work items carrying a spec.reason, which says nothing about how often a scan drops a row. It is out of this rationale entirely. The 384 lane caught (a) and made (b); both corrections are recorded in WRONG_CALLS 2026-08-26c.

THE CLASS, AND WHY A RATCHET RATHER THAN A SWEEP. [MEASURED 2026-08-26] 207 unmarked cursor-loop scan swallows in 127 files tree-wide (a `rows.Scan` inside a `for rows.Next()` loop whose error branch continues), 166 of them in platform/orchestration/actions/**. Converting 207 sites blind would be a worse change than the bug. More decisively, THE SHAPE IS NOT THE DEFECT: at least one baseline site — scanBlogArticles itself — has this exact shape AND a correct guard, because the guard lives after the loop. A ban would convict the estate's own best precedent. So the ratchet pins per-file COUNTS with strict equality: a count that rises or a new file fails ('close the door'); a count that FALLS also fails, with an instruction to lower the baseline ('ratchet down'), so the baseline cannot drift and a net-zero swap cannot hide. An at-site opt-out `// scan-loss:accepted: <reason>` keeps the reason next to the code. Two layers, one pattern, per work_item_type_minting_ratchet_test.go's own rule: a BLOCKING Go source-sensor over the actions package, and an ADVISORY pattern-check.py twin that is tree-wide because the 41 out-of-package sites have no blocking cover — and both read the SAME baseline file, which is tighter than the minting pair (which shares only a regex). Classifier parity between the two readers is verified: 207/127 from both, zero disagreements, plus six shared edge cases (marked/unmarked, return-vs-continue, non-default cursor name, comment prose, single-row QueryRow).

EVERY GUARD CARRIES THE MUTATION DISCIPLINE, RUN RATHER THAN PROMISED. ScanShortfall body -> `return nil`: TestScanShortfall_ShortfallIsAnError goes red (verified). Delete the ScanShortfall call and restore `return out, rows.Err()`: both loader refusal tests go red, reporting '1 section(s) with no error' and '(0 sections, nil error)' — i.e. the mutation reproduces the original defect verbatim (verified). Remove a baseline line: ratchet reports NEW sites (verified). Inflate a baseline count: ratchet reports FELL / ratchet down (verified). The classifier has its own StillBites test because a source sensor whose pattern is neutered matches nothing and passes for ever, which looks exactly like a clean tree.

STATED RESIDUALS, so nothing here reads as wider coverage than it has: (1) the 41 sites outside platform/orchestration/actions are advisory-only; (2) CONTENT loss is a different axis and is NOT covered — loadStoredSections' own `_ = json.Unmarshal(cdJSON, &s.contentData)` keeps the row and empties it on corrupt JSON, so offered == kept and no count guard can see it; it is commented at the site and recorded in the bug file; (3) the ratchet tracks the SHAPE, so it cannot tell whether a guard that exists is also consulted; (4) scanBlogArticles is left unconverted — it is already guarded, and a behaviour-neutral refactor of the listing rebuild would widen a bug fix's blast radius for nothing.

plan.summary: Add one shared guard, datahelpers.ScanShortfall(offered, kept, subject), comparing rows the cursor yielded to rows kept — never a second query, so it is invariant to the query's own legitimate filtering and cannot race a concurrent write. Apply it STRICTLY in loadStoredSections (any loss errors, before anything is written) because that reader feeds a wholesale replace, making a partial result destruction rather than degradation. Then close the door on the class with a per-file-count ratchet: a blocking Go source sensor over platform/orchestration/actions/** and an advisory pattern-check.py twin tree-wide, both reading one shared baseline, with an at-site `// scan-loss:accepted: <reason>` opt-out for deliberate guarded loss.

edits.rationale: One implementation of 'did this row scan lose anything the query gave me', so the guard is not 225 hand-copies. Ships exactly ONE function, the strict one, because that is the policy the first caller exercises — a graded twin shipped 'for completeness' would be a mechanism nobody runs, which this estate objects to by name. The doc comment pins WHICH count and why the intuitive version dies in production, and names scanBlogArticles as the graded sibling that can adopt the counters when next touched.

Four cases, two of which exist to stop the guard being over-eager rather than to prove it fires: zero offered is an empty table not a loss, and kept exceeding offered is a legitimate fan-out. A guard that refuses correct input gets loosened and then removed — the failure mode the bug file pins. Mutation comment states: replace the body with `return nil` and the shortfall test must fail.

The motivating site. Counts rows the cursor yielded, keeps the per-row Warn and continue deliberately (on a mixed failure it records EVERY failing row's cause, where an immediate return records only the first — and the first is rarely the informative one when a projection has drifted), then refuses at the end. Strict rather than graded because save_page_sections replaces the page's rows wholesale, so a dropped section is DELETED. The refusal lands before any write, so a page keeps serving its last good render while the step fails and retries. The caller already propagates (rerender_page_sections_action.go:270, `return nil, fmt.Errorf("load stored sections: %w", err)`), verified — so this is not a guard whose error its own caller re-swallows.

Four sqlmock cases against loadStoredSections directly: partial loss refuses and names the shortfall; TOTAL loss errors rather than returning ([], nil) — the bd811fa93 shape; healthy rows are all kept (the guard must not fire on correct input); an empty page is not a loss. The header names the seven red tests BY NAME (they have moved twice; the bug file's own correction records a line number expiring the same afternoon) and records the sqlmock ExpectationsWereMet detail. It also states how rows are poisoned (NULL into `position`, an int) and warns that if position ever becomes nullable or COALESCEd, THIS TEST GOES GREEN FOR THE WRONG REASON — pick another non-nullable destination rather than deleting it.

grounded_in: The defect, verbatim at the symbol (cited by symbol because this file's line numbers expired the same afternoon the bug was filed) — [platform/orchestration/actions/rerender_page_sections_action.go, loadStoredSections]: "if err := rows.Scan(&s.id, &s.parentInstanceID, &s.componentID, &s.slotName, &cdJSON, &s.renderedHTML, &s.position, &s.componentVersionID); err != nil { logger.Warn("rerender_page_sections: row scan failed", zap.Error(err)); continue }  ... return out, rows.Err()"

Why STRICT and not graded: the loss is destructive, not degrading. Verified first-hand rather than inherited from the plan that proposed it. — [platform/orchestration/actions/save_page_sections_action.go:898 — and rerender_page_sections_removed_test.go's header: 'save_page_sections then replaces the page's rows wholesale']: "DELETE FROM page_components WHERE page_id = $1 AND ..."

The precedent this fix propagates, and it was REQUIRED BY A SEAT rather than volunteered — the first cut logged-and-skipped unconditionally — [platform/orchestration/actions/rebuild_blog_listing_action.go, scanBlogArticles (council round 170147b4, bug_historian — provenance supplied by the bugs_open/384 lane)]: "if attempted > 0 && len(articles) == 0 { logger.Error("RebuildBlogListingAction: EVERY blog post row failed to scan — the projection's column list no longer matches the Scan destinations; refusing to report an empty listing as 'no posts'", ...); return nil, fmt.Errorf("blog listing scan failed for all %d offered rows (%d scan errors): the query projection and the Scan destinations have diverged", attempted, scanFailures) }"

The second precedent: the same count-guard reasoning, already council-mandated in this package — [platform/orchestration/actions/validate_page_content_surface_sections.go, collectPageSections (council round 3ed2b792, bug_historian)]: "The guard is now a count rather than a shape test, which is why it is strong: if the canonical reader returns fewer sections than the metadata array held, SOMETHING was dropped ... and we refuse component grain for the whole page."

Blast radius measured AT THE SCAN: zero by schema, not by luck. The column-by-column analysis is the argument; this query is its control. — [live clients_db, 2026-08-26; \d page_components confirms `position integer NOT NULL` and `id uuid NOT NULL`]: "SELECT count(*) AS rows_live, count(*) FILTER (WHERE position IS NULL) AS null_position, count(*) FILTER (WHERE content_data IS NULL) AS null_content_data FROM page_components WHERE build_status IS DISTINCT FROM 'removed';  -->  2194 | 0 | 54"

The class size and why a ratchet rather than a sweep. Note the number is 207, not the 225 an earlier looser classifier reported — that version also counted single-row QueryRow(...).Scan(&x) in a loop, which is not this shape. — [census over the tree, 2026-08-26; baseline at platform/orchestration/actions/scan_swallow_baseline.txt]: "207 unmarked cursor-loop scan swallows in 127 files across platform/ internal/ pkg/ cmd/; 166 in platform/orchestration/actions/**, 41 outside it. Classifier parity between the Go and Python readers verified: 207/127 from both, zero disagreements."

The reproduction, and why the covering tests could not have caught it (supplied and verified by the news_editorial lane, who own those tests) — [commit bd811fa93; rerender_page_sections_resolve_test.go and save_sections_stored_slot_identity_test.go]: "Those seven assert section COUNT and CONTENT, never rows-in-equals-rows-out, so they would have PASSED on a column change that was wrong in a way that still scanned. They also call mock.ExpectationsWereMet(), so sqlmock's own completeness assertion ran and passed: the query was issued exactly as expected, and only the scan silently produced nothing."

The estate rule this fix obeys for its two layers — [platform/orchestration/actions/work_item_type_minting_ratchet_test.go, header]: "scripts/pattern-check.py carries the same regex as check_dynamic_item_type and was extended in the same commit — but pattern-check is ADVISORY BY DESIGN ... which is what a Go test does and an advisory cannot. Two layers, one pattern: change them TOGETHER."
plan.risks:
(1) STRICT policy on the fleet's busiest pipeline. Mitigated and MEASURED rather than asserted: the guard cannot fire on any state the database can currently hold (every projected column NOT NULL, COALESCEd, or NULL-safe []byte), so day-one firing rate is zero by construction. It can only fire on a projection/destination divergence, which is a code defect — and in that case it fails ALL rows, where strict and graded behave identically anyway. The refusal lands before any write, so the page keeps serving its last good render. STATED LIMIT: this expires if the projection or schema changes; a nullable un-COALESCEd column added to that SELECT falsifies it. The news_editorial lane, who are adding columns there, have accepted this as a constraint on their change.

(2) The baseline could be hand-edited to silence a red ratchet. Partly mitigated: a count that FALLS also fails, so the baseline cannot drift upward-then-back, and TestScanSwallowBaselineMatchesThisPackage logs the pinned total. Not fully closed — someone determined can still lower a count and delete a guard in one commit. That is a review surface, not a mechanical one, and it is stated rather than papered over.

(3) The two classifiers could drift apart, which would make 'one baseline, two readers' a lie. Mitigated by verified parity at submission time (207/127 both, zero disagreements, plus six shared edge cases) and by both headers naming the other. NOT mechanically enforced — there is no test that runs the Python classifier from Go. A parity test would need a Python invocation from the Go suite; recorded as the honest residual rather than claimed.

(4) CONTENT loss is not covered and must not read as covered. loadStoredSections' `_ = json.Unmarshal(cdJSON, &s.contentData)` keeps the row and empties it on corrupt JSON, so offered == kept. Commented at the site, recorded in bugs_open/410, explicitly listed in the ratchet header's 'what it cannot see'.

(5) The 41 sites outside platform/orchestration/actions have ADVISORY cover only. A blocking test walking the whole tree from inside one package is fragile; that population is not artefact-shaped. Stated in the ratchet header rather than left to look like full coverage.
